title: Global Verdier duality
statement:
Let $X$ be smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected of
pure dimension $d$ over $k$ (no admissibility hypothesis on $a_X$: its
exceptional adjoint is the unconditional one of [sk-def-sf-operations](vi)).
Assume either that $X$ is proper, or that
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ for a smooth, separated finite-type, geometrically
connected $k_0$-scheme $X_0$; in the latter case no properness is required.
For $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
\RG_c(X,K)^\vee\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\RG\bigl(X,\mathbb D_XK\bigr),
$$

in the point category $\Dbc(s,\Lambda)$ of def:weil-finite-coefficient-point,
natural in $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and compatible with finite reduction, scalar
extension and shifts; for $K=\Lambda_X$ it reads
$\RG_c(X,\Lambda)^\vee\cong\RG(X,\omega_X)$.

proof.text: Specialize the existing Verdier exchange theorem to a_X:X→Spec k. Apply lem-sf-global-identity-normalization to obtain normalized closed structures and the evaluation-transposed epsilon as a natural transformation with signed shifts and coefficient equations, but no inverse.

For each K and test object T, compose the inverse point tensor-Hom bijection, precomposition by the projection isomorphism, exceptional adjunction, the identity dualizing comparison, tensor-Hom on X and pull/star adjunction. Projection naturality and adjunction naturality prove naturality in T. Apply isoOfNaturalHomEquiv to the resulting Hom bijections. Expansion at the identity shows that its hom is exactly StageData.epsilon. Thus every epsilon component is invertible. Promote the recorded transformation to StageConclusion, retaining exactly its shifts.

For the tensor-Hom adjunction at the tensor unit, compare its right adjoint with the identity using Adjunction.rightAdjointUniq and the right-unitor adjunction. The counit equation gives exactly inverse right unitor followed by evaluation; the reverse comparison is exactly the transpose of the right unitor. These comparisons are inverse. Compose this unit isomorphism with the same epsilon component, then assemble Package from the normalized ring, projection, unit, signed-shift and coefficient records.

proof_origin.place: T2 Lean reduction: identity normalization, explicit Yoneda invertibility via the five adjunction bijections, and tensor-unit evaluation identities.

blueprint_update.statement:
Here $\mathbb D_X$ and $\omega_X=a_X^!\Lambda_s$ are the Verdier dual and the dualizing
complex of [sk-def-ops], and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$.

Over algebraically closed $k$, every
$K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ has natural isomorphisms in
$\Perf(\Lambda)$

$$
 R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK)\simeq
 R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(R\Gamma_c(X,K),\Lambda),
 \tag{1}
$$

$$
 R\Gamma_c(X,\mathbb D_XK)\simeq
 R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(R\Gamma(X,K),\Lambda).
 \tag{2}
$$

The first is the adjoint of the pairing formed by mixed-support cup
product, evaluation, and the counit $\epsilon_{a_X}$ of
$Ra_{X!}\dashv a_X^!$:

$$
 R\Gamma_c(X,K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}R\Gamma(X,\mathbb D_XK)
 \longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,\omega_X)
 \xrightarrow{\epsilon_{a_X}}\Lambda.
$$

For a finite base field the same isomorphisms hold in
$D(s_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$, before passage to the geometric fibre.

proof.text:
Take $f=a_X$ in the two Verdier exchanges ([sk-thm-sf-verdier-exchange]). On a geometric
point the dualizing object is $\Lambda$, and
[sk-lem-finite] identifies $\Dctf(s,\Lambda)$ with
$\Perf(\Lambda)$. The first exchange
was constructed from exactly the indicated evaluation and counit,
so it identifies the adjoint of that pairing, including its signs.
The second exchange gives the second formula. Equivalently, it
follows by applying the first formula to $\mathbb D_XK$ and
dualizing perfect complexes. A detailed account of this theorem is in
the blueprint chapters on six functors and Poincaré duality (PDBP).
